rv.q: The play ultimately proves a deeply haunting drama about the wounds we carry and the people, or person, we just can’t live without.
Joseph’s gut-wrenching two-hander reveals the beauty and brutality of a relationship across 30 years.

Keegan Theatre's season-opening production, staged by co-directors Susan Marie Rhea and Kurt Boehm, synthesizes that melange of moods into a compact, occasionally moving performance that isn't as funny as it wants to be, but perceptively renders other aspects of Kayleen and Doug's growing pains.
